_Posted by Kunal's robot (Claude Opus 5.5) ↓_
>
> ## Motivation
>
> `wrap_shm_features()` copies each decoded feature tensor into a POSIX shared-memory segment. It runs on the tokenizer manager's event loop, so a request with several large images holds the loop, and `/health` with it, for the length of the copy.
>
> ```
> before:  loop  [tokenize][===== shm copy =====][send]
> after:   loop  [tokenize]  ...serves others...  [send]
>          pool             [===== shm copy =====]
> ```
>
> ## Modifications
>
> - Run the copy in the default executor, the same way the CUDA VMM transport already publishes features.
> - Unlink the segments if the request is cancelled mid-copy. The unlink hangs on the copy future as a done callback, as the VMM path does, so a second cancellation while the task waits for the copy (a client disconnect cancels through the server's cancel scope) cannot skip it.
> - The copy is one more await before dispatch, so a request aborted during it is dropped and its segments released, the way the abort check after the other awaits drops one (#47546).
> - Any exit from `_send_one_request` before dispatch, a cancellation during the copy included, returns the CUDA IPC leases preprocessing took, since no consumer will acknowledge them.
> - Add five tests to `test_gpu_feature_transport.py`: the loop stays responsive during the copy, cancellation unlinks the segments, a second cancellation still unlinks them, an abort during the copy skips dispatch and unlinks them, and a cancellation during the copy returns the CUDA IPC leases. The last three fail without the matching change.
>
> This PR is independent of #44574 and #44576, which address the same workload.
>
> ## Accuracy Tests
>
> Not applicable: the copied bytes are unchanged.
>
> ## Speed Tests and Profiling
>
> The tensor copy releases the GIL. Copying 40 MB left a 1.4 ms worst-case event-loop gap from a worker thread, against 12 ms on the loop.
>
> End to end, together with #44574 and #44576, see the table in #44574.
>
> ## Checklist
>
> - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
> - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
> - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). Not needed.
> - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep SHM cleanup alive after repeated cancellation**

When a request is cancelled a second time while the executor is still copying (for example, task cancellation followed by loop shutdown), this unshielded `await future` is interrupted and cancels only the asyncio wrapper; the already-running worker still returns a tokenized object containing named `ShmPointerMMData` segments, but `discard_shm_features` is never called. Those segments deliberately are not unlinked by `__del__`, so repeated cases can fill `/dev/shm` until process exit. Attach cleanup as a done callback or otherwise make it survive subsequent cancellation, as the CUDA VMM publication path does.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Release CUDA IPC leases on cancelled SHM wrapping**

When `--mm-feature-transport=cuda_ipc` is enabled and a client disconnects while this executor job is pending, preprocessing has already replaced GPU tensors with `CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy` leases, but this handler only schedules `discard_shm_features`, which ignores those proxies. `_send_one_request`'s `finally` only cancels VMM and positional transports, and because the scheduler never receives this request no consumer acknowledges the CUDA IPC leases; repeated cancellations therefore permanently occupy the bounded pool and force later requests onto the CPU fallback. Call `_cancel_cuda_ipc_features((tokenized_obj,))` on this cancellation path as the abort path does.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Initialize mm_processor in the failed-dispatch fixture**

When the registered CPU suite runs `TestCudaVmmFeatureTransport.test_failed_dispatch_cancels_published_items`, its manager is created via `object.__new__` and sets no `mm_processor`. This new cleanup enters `_cancel_cuda_ipc_features`, whose first expression evaluates `self.mm_processor`, so the expected `RuntimeError("send failed")` is replaced by `AttributeError` and the test deterministically fails. Initialize `manager.mm_processor` in that fixture (as the new `_dispatching_manager` helper does), or make the lookup tolerate an absent manager attribute.

_Posted by Kunal's robot (Claude Fable 5.1) ↓_
>
> Right, that fixture reaches the new cleanup without an `mm_processor`. d87c1b71e0 sets one on it. The whole of `test_gpu_feature_transport.py` passes locally now (39 tests).

+        """A task cancelled again while it waits for the copy to finish (a client
+        disconnect cancels through the server's cancel scope) must still release
+        the segments the copy produced."""
+        from sglang.srt.managers import tokenizer_manager
+
+        manager = object.__new__(tokenizer_manager.TokenizerManager)
+        tokenized_obj = self._tokenized_obj()
+        wrap_started = threading.Event()
+        release_wrap = threading.Event()
+
+        def wrap(obj):
+            wrap_started.set()
+            release_wrap.wait()
+            return obj
+
+        async def cancel_twice_mid_wrap():
+            task = asyncio.create_task(manager._wrap_shm_features_async(tokenized_obj))
+            await asyncio.to_thread(wrap_started.wait)
+            task.cancel()
+            await asyncio.sleep(0)
+            task.cancel()
+            release_wrap.set()
+            with self.assertRaises(asyncio.CancelledError):
+                await task

+            patch.object(tokenizer_manager, "wrap_shm_features", wrap),
+            patch.object(tokenizer_manager, "discard_shm_features", discard),
+        ):

+
+        discard.assert_called_once_with(tokenized_obj)
+

+        """A request aborted while its features copy to shared memory is not
+        dispatched, since the scheduler drops an abort for a rid it has not seen,
+        and the segments the copy produced are released."""

+

+    def test_cancelled_copy_returns_cuda_ipc_leases(self):

+            await asyncio.to_thread(wrap_started.wait)

+            patch.object(tokenizer_manager, "discard_shm_features", MagicMock()),

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep SHM cleanup alive after repeated cancellation**

When a request is cancelled a second time while the executor is still copying (for example, task cancellation followed by loop shutdown), this unshielded `await future` is interrupted and cancels only the asyncio wrapper; the already-running worker still returns a tokenized object containing named `ShmPointerMMData` segments, but `discard_shm_features` is never called. Those segments deliberately are not unlinked by `__del__`, so repeated cases can fill `/dev/shm` until process exit. Attach cleanup as a done callback or otherwise make it survive subsequent cancellation, as the CUDA VMM publication path does.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Release CUDA IPC leases on cancelled SHM wrapping**

When `--mm-feature-transport=cuda_ipc` is enabled and a client disconnects while this executor job is pending, preprocessing has already replaced GPU tensors with `CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy` leases, but this handler only schedules `discard_shm_features`, which ignores those proxies. `_send_one_request`'s `finally` only cancels VMM and positional transports, and because the scheduler never receives this request no consumer acknowledges the CUDA IPC leases; repeated cancellations therefore permanently occupy the bounded pool and force later requests onto the CPU fallback. Call `_cancel_cuda_ipc_features((tokenized_obj,))` on this cancellation path as the abort path does.
